name: Santo Domingo Albarradas Zapotec
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Adam, Christopher. 2003. A study of Dihidx Bilyahab (Santo Domingo Albarradas Zapotec) morphophonology (Glottolog hhtype: phonology) — not found online; SIL/UND repositories Cloudflare-blocked.

new_statements.quote: There are simple and complex syllable nuclei; the complex nuclei subdivide into laryngealized (aa), interrupted (aʔ), and aspirated (ah) nuclei. Syllables are either stressed or unstressed. There are three tonemes: rising, falling, and low. In unstressed syllables there is neutralization of the rising and falling tones to a phonetic high pitch. Tone is not written in this paper. However, where two morphemes are distinguished only by their inherent toneme, one of them is marked by a diacritic accent.
new_statements.citation: Kreikebaum, Wolfram. 1987. Fronting and related features in Santo Domingo Albarradas Zapotec. SIL-Mexico Workpapers 9: 33-71. Mexico: Summer Institute of Linguistics.
new_statements.locator: p. 33 (introductory phonology paragraph, unnumbered; PDF p. 2 of; same page in p. 1)
new_statements.reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.rule_in_words: The language is tonal (three tonemes per Kreikebaum 1987; four tones high/low/rising/falling per Buck 1973 reporting Eunice Pike) and has a stressed/unstressed distinction among syllables, with tonal contrasts (rising vs falling) neutralized in unstressed syllables. Neither source states where stress falls in the word; no positional rule is available from any accessible description.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. Kreikebaum notes 'considerable subdialectal and idiolectal variation' in SDA (p. 33); Buck 1973 p. 5 notes stem+clitic words show 'change of stress' and different syllable rhythm, and p. 7 gives tone sandhi (rising/falling simplify before a following word).
new_statements.domain_note: Word/syllable level in Kreikebaum (phoneme-inventory paragraph); Buck 1973 concerns isolated one- and two-syllable words read from lists plus phrase-level tone sandhi. Word position of stress is not stated by either.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe the Santo Domingo Albarradas variety (Kreikebaum's 'SDA'; Buck 1973 'Santo Domingo Zapotec', speaker Juan de Dios Martínez; Adam's 'Dihidx Bilyáhab'), i.e. sant1450 / zas. Kreikebaum 1987 p. 33 says Albarradas Zapotec is also spoken in Santa María and San Miguel Albarradas, while 'the speech of Santa Catarina Albarradas is somewhat different' (that is sant1448, Santa Catarina Albarradas Zapotec, ztn). SDA has 'considerable subdialectal and idiolectal variation' (Kreikebaum 1987: 33; Language Lessons note idiolectal loss of fortis/lenis lateral and nasal contrasts).

sources.citation: Buck, Marjorie J. 1973. Lesson in reading tone: Santo Domingo Zapoteco. Notes on Literacy 15: 9-15 (SIL; 2018 re-typeset PDF).
sources.note: Literacy report of Eunice Pike teaching a Santo Domingo speaker to read tone: 'In Santo Domingo Zapotec there are four tones—high, low, rising, [and] falling' (p. 7); mentions tone sandhi and that stem+clitic words 'with change of stress are also difficult' (p. 5). No stress-placement rule.
